title: Pull every fourth part off an indexing line for QC, counting identical parts as they pass
instruction: Parts will ride past on the conveyor one at a time. Take every fourth part off the line and put it in the blue QC tray, counting the first part to arrive as part 1 (so the 4th and the 8th), and let all the others ride past.
context: Sampling plans pull every nth part off a running line for measurement, so drift is caught across the whole run. The parts are identical and the line hides them before and after the station, so the only way to pick the right ones is to keep count as they pass. Done by: line operators and quality inspectors.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (1.10 x 1.30 m) whose edges are 65 cm either side of the midpoint between the bases. A straight indexing conveyor crosses the table parallel to the line through the bases. Its centre line is 32 cm in front of the bases, and it runs from 68 cm right to 88 cm left of the midpoint. Past the table's left edge it stands on a dark steel post (11 x 4 cm, table height) whose centre is 84 cm left of the midpoint. Two dark steel rails (1.5 x 1.5 cm, 156 cm long) run 2 cm either side of the centre line. A grey sheet-steel cover hides the line except one open window, which runs from 5 to 15 cm left of the midpoint and is open from the table up. Either side of the window, the cover is a tunnel 73 cm long and 11 cm wide outside: two 1 cm side walls 9.2 cm tall, their inner faces 4.5 cm either side of the centre line, under a 0.8 cm roof, closed at the outer end. Eight grey steel carriers (6.5 x 6.5 x 1.5 cm) ride 2 mm above the rails, square to them, nose to tail 9 cm apart (centre to centre). At the start, carrier k (k = 1 to 8) is centred k x 9 cm to the right of the window's centre, all under the right tunnel, and the window is empty. Each carrier has one bare aluminium cube (4 x 4 x 4 cm, 170 g) lying in its middle, square to it. The cubes are identical, except that each has its number (1 to 8, matching its carrier) engraved on its underside. A blue plastic open tray (17 x 17 cm outside, 15 x 15 cm inside, 1 cm floor, 4 cm walls) stands square on the table. Its centre is 16 cm in front of the bases and 33 cm left of the midpoint. The line's motion, from the start of the trial: it stands still for 3.0 s. Then every 4.0 s it moves all carriers together 9 cm to the left in 1.2 s (smooth start and stop, peak speed 11.8 cm/s). After each move, the next carrier stands in the window for 2.8 s. The line moves 9 times in all, so cube 1 stands in the window from 4.2 to 7.0 s and cube 8 from 32.2 to 35.0 s. After the 9th move (35.0 to 36.2 s) the line stops with every carrier under the left tunnel and the window empty.
scoring: At the end of the trial: 0.5 for each of cubes 4 and 8 lying in the tray (centre inside the tray's walls, underside within 1 cm of the tray floor, still), minus 0.25 for each other cube taken off the line (anywhere but lying on a carrier: in the tray, on the table, in a gripper), never below 0. So 1.0 if exactly cubes 4 and 8 are in the tray and every other cube still rides on a carrier (the trial ends with success once this has held for 1 s); 0.75 with both samples and one wrong cube taken; 0.5 with one sample; 0.25 with one sample and one wrong cube taken; 0 otherwise (for example nothing taken, every cube taken, or cubes 3 and 7 taken). A cube counts as itself whenever it was taken, but only the cube standing in the window can be reached: the others are under the cover.
reset_notes: Run the carriers back so carrier k is k x 9 cm right of the window's centre, put cube k on carrier k, number down, and start the line's timer with the trial. To score, read the numbers under the cubes in the tray, then lift the left tunnel's cover and count the cubes still on carriers.
fidelity: The carriers follow the line's path exactly, like a stiff servo-driven indexing conveyor: the arms can't push them or stop them, where a real line would stop on a jam. They ride 2 mm above the rails. The cubes have the station's rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than aluminium on steel. At a peak acceleration under 0.4 m/s², they don't slide on the carriers. The cover is rigid.
